text:
emma: Hey team — opened a PR to add VPC peering (prod <-> analytics), migrate analytics NATs to vpc-central, and add a Secrets Manager PrivateLink iface. PR: https://gitlab.redwood/infra/merge_requests/421. Looking for quick reviews on route propagation, terraform import steps, and endpoint type (iface vs gateway).

ajay: :eyes: I can review. quick q: are we touching public subnets or only private route tables?

emma: only private. Plan is: create aws_vpc_peering_connection, accept it, add aws_route entries in both VPCs' private route tables, and replace analytics nat-gw references to point at central per-AZ NATs. No changes to IGWs or public subnets.

sophia: heads up — peering does NOT auto-propagate to route tables. you need explicit aws_route per route table (or RT propagation via TGW if we had one). Also interface endpoints are correct for Secrets Manager/SSM. gateway endpoints are for S3/Dynamo.

marcus: are the VPCs in the same account? if different accounts, we need the accept role in the other account. Also watch CIDR overlap — terraform import will fail if overlaps.

emma: same account. CIDRs: prod 10.10.0.0/16, analytics 10.20.0.0/16, central 10.254.0.0/16 — no overlap. I imported the peering object locally to avoid recreation: `terraform import module.network.aws_vpc_peering_connection.peering pcx-0abc123456789`. Plan looks good; main changes are route additions and some route_table_association updates. Pasted plan excerpt below.

emma: ```
# plan excerpt
+ aws_vpc_peering_connection.peering (imported)
+ aws_route.analytics-to-prod[0] (new) will add route to analytics-private-rt-a -> 10.10.0.0/16 via pcx-0abc123456789
+ aws_route.prod-to-analytics[0] (new) will add route to prod-private-rt-a -> 10.20.0.0/16 via pcx-0abc123456789
~ aws_route_table_association.analytics-private-rt-a (updated)
  - association of subnets -> updated to include route
```

ajay: thanks. small suggestions: 1) add a comment in tf to call out manual import step so future runs don't try to recreate. 2) consider `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [ route_table_id ] }` only if we’re swapping associations outside terraform — but probably not needed here.

infra-bot: terraform plan: 8 to add, 2 to change, 0 to destroy. No drift detected for critical network resources. (run-id: t-plan-20251012-07)

sophia: also add a short rollback/runbook: if something breaks we can remove the two new routes in analytics to cut traffic back to prod, or revert to per-AZ nat-gws by restoring previous route targets. Test in staging before prod.

emma: will add runbook and a brief test checklist to the MR. planning to apply in staging tomorrow morning and do a canary for one AZ. I'll ping once staging apply is green. Thanks for the pointers :thumbsup:

ajay: :shipit: ping me when you want me to approve the MR.

marcus: add an acceptance test to verify cross-vpc DNS resolution (internal names) — service discovery sometimes surprises folks after peering.

emma: good call. I'll include a small curl/test script and a note about cross-vpc DNS. final MR update incoming.
